body.en: Beyond linear equations, the EST II tests rational expressions, absolute value equations, and advanced polynomial manipulation.

Systems and inequalities

Graphical solutions of systems of inequalities define a feasible region. To find vertices, solve pairs of boundary lines simultaneously. EST II questions may ask for the maximum or minimum of a linear expression over the feasible region — an introduction to linear programming.

Polynomial long division: divide \(p(x)\) by \(d(x)\) to get quotient \(q(x)\) and remainder \(r(x)\). Rational equations: multiply through by LCD, then solve, checking for extraneous solutions. Logarithmic equations: use log laws to combine terms, then convert to exponential form.

label.en: Worked example — Rational equation with extraneous solution

body.en:
Solve \(\dfrac{x}{x-2} + \dfrac{1}{x+2} = \dfrac{8}{x^2-4}\).

LCD \(= (x-2)(x+2)\). Multiply through: \(x(x+2)+(x-2) = 8\).

\(x^2+2x+x-2 = 8 \Rightarrow x^2+3x-10 = 0 \Rightarrow (x+5)(x-2)=0\).

\(x=2\) is extraneous (denominator = 0). Solution: \(x = -5\).

figure.title: Nonlinear System: Parabola y = x² - 4x + 3 and Line y = -2x + 6

caption.en: Graphical representation of the nonlinear system \(y = x^2 - 4x + 3\) and \(y = -2x + 6\). The parabola and line intersect at \((-1, 8)\) and \((3, 0)\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Rational Equations & Polynomial Theorems

body.en:
• Extraneous Solutions in Rational Equations: When multiplying across by the LCD, you may introduce solutions that make an original denominator zero. Always substitute candidate solutions back into the original denominators to verify they are non-zero.
  • Remainder Theorem Sign Inversion: When dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - c)\), the remainder is \(P(c)\). But when dividing by \((x + c)\), the divisor is \((x - (-c))\), so the remainder is \(P(-c)\). Misplacing this minus sign is the #1 error on EST II polynomial questions.
  • Absolute Value Inequalities: \(|x - a| \le b\) translates to the compound inequality \(-b \le x - a \le b\) (an intersection/interval). In contrast, \(|x - a| \ge b\) translates to \(x - a \le -b\) OR \(x - a \ge b\) (a union of disjoint rays).
  • Nonlinear Systems Intersection Count: When solving a system of a parabola \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) and line \(y = mx + k\), substitute to obtain a single quadratic. Check the discriminant \(\Delta = B^2 - 4AC\): \(\Delta > 0\) gives 2 real solutions, \(\Delta = 0\) gives 1 tangent point, and \(\Delta < 0\) gives no real intersections.

question.en: Solve the nonlinear system of equations: \[ \begin{cases} y = x^2 - 4x + 3 \\ 2x + y = 6 \end{cases} \] Find all points of intersection \((x, y)\).

solution.en:
Substitution: Express \(y\) from the linear equation: \(y = 6 - 2x\). Substitute into the quadratic: \[ 6 - 2x = x^2 - 4x + 3 \implies x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0. \]

Factoring: \[ (x - 3)(x + 1) = 0 \implies x_1 = 3,\quad x_2 = -1. \]

Find corresponding \(y\) values:

  • For \(x = 3\): \(y = 6 - 2(3) = 0\) → \((3, 0)\).
  • For \(x = -1\): \(y = 6 - 2(-1) = 8\) → \((-1, 8)\).

The two intersection points are \((3, 0)\) and \((-1, 8)\).
